doc.name: A — vinyl catalogue, hands in frame, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: 180g vinyl record and inner sleeve
Category: vinyl
Shot programme: hands in frame
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the art director signing off every frame of this vinyl campaign. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the hero three-quarter in a hands in frame treatment.

SUBJECT. A 180g vinyl record and inner sleeve. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Three-quarter hero angle at label height with the product a touch above eye line. Shoot on an 85mm short telephoto at f/1.8, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with an overcast soft dome with no directional shadow at all. Stage the product on or against cast pigmented resin, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
